beats.text: 1492 began with a surrender and a promise. The promise didn't last.
By 1491, Granada was the last Muslim kingdom in Spain, after nearly eight centuries of al-Andalus. It was under siege.
beats.say: By fourteen ninety-one, Granada was the last Muslim kingdom in Spain, after nearly eight centuries of al-Andalus. It was under siege.

beats.text: Its sultan, Boabdil, negotiated. Muslims could keep their mosques, their laws, their faith. Isabella and Ferdinand signed.
On the second of January 1492, Boabdil handed over the keys of the city.
beats.say: On the second of January fourteen ninety-two, Boabdil handed over the keys of the city.

beats.text: Legend says he looked back from a mountain pass and wept. That spot is still called the Moor's Last Sigh.
Three months later, the same monarchs signed the Alhambra Decree. Spain's Jews had four months: convert, or leave.
Tens of thousands left homes their families had lived in for over a thousand years. Their descendants, the Sephardim, still speak Ladino, a form of old Spanish.
And the promise to Granada's Muslims? Within ten years, they too were told: convert, or leave.
But that same spring, an Italian sailor was waiting for an answer from the queen.

beats.sub: Follow so you don't miss it
